title: Critical dyadic-band reduction for upper resets

concepts.label: critical dyadic band index
concepts.note: The nearest transition of indexed dyadic powers across a reset charge.

concepts.label: generic dyadic-band escape
concepts.note: Avoidance of all forbidden dyadic intervals and its one-index certificate.

concepts.label: actual upper-reset charge
concepts.note: The concrete seam charge bounded by the top dyadic boundary.

concepts.label: critical-band producer
concepts.note: The open global producer requiring a certified critical gap at every late upper reset.

concepts.label: Mersenne half-membership endpoint
concepts.note: The conditional endpoint obtained by transport to the existing all-band consumer.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: CriticalDyadicBandIndex d E j means j≤d, E≤2^(d-j+1), and either j=d or 2^(d-(j+1)+1)<E. It records a transition index where the indexed dyadic powers pass from at least E to below E.
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Pure natural-number dyadic interval normalisation used internally by this corpus; no priority or novelty search has been performed.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The definition encodes a transition index but does not by itself prove a separately stated uniqueness theorem or a critical gap.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If E≤2^(d+1), avoidance for every j≤d of the forbidden interval E<2^(d-j+1)<E+2(d+j) is equivalent to the existence of one CriticalDyadicBandIndex j with E+2(d+j)≤2^(d-j+1).
statement_nodes.engine: nearest-boundary classification of a finite descending dyadic sequence
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Pure natural-number dyadic interval normalisation used internally by this corpus; no priority or novelty search has been performed.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The equivalence assumes E≤2^(d+1) and reduces quantifiers; it does not prove the required gap and is not a strength reduction.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: For d≥5, whenever the concrete seam adjacent cut is an upper reset, its charge seamUpperResetCharge=4*overshoot+abovePulse is at most 2^(d+1).
statement_nodes.engine: the concrete upper-reset inequality and exact pulse/overshoot charge definition
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Corpus-specific seam specialisation; no historical priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The theorem applies only under successorCarries. It supplies admissibility for the generic collapse, not avoidance of any band.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: SeamUpperResetCriticalBandEscape, requiring one certified critical gap at every late upper reset, is logically equivalent to SeamUpperResetDyadicBandEscape, which requires every indexed band escape.
statement_nodes.engine: rowwise specialization of the generic critical-index equivalence using the actual reset-charge bound
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Corpus-specific seam specialisation and transport; no historical priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The equivalence is an exact coordinate reformulation. Neither global producer is proved, and finite row checks do not discharge the universal late-row quantifier.

statement_nodes.canonical_statement: If SeamUpperResetCriticalBandEscape holds, then 1/2 belongs to the Mersenne achievement set; the proof transports the critical producer through the exact equivalence and applies the existing all-band consumer.
open_antecedents: SeamUpperResetCriticalBandEscape: at every d≥13 that is an upper reset, there exists a critical index whose nearest dyadic boundary has margin at least 2(d+j) above the reset charge.
statement_nodes.engine: producer equivalence followed by the existing all-band half-membership consumer
statement_nodes.prior_art_note: Corpus-specific conditional transport; no historical priority claim is made.
statement_nodes.scope_caveat: The producer is unproved. The theorem neither establishes half-membership nor refutes the universal statement in Erdős #257, and it proves no equidistribution statement.

intra_zone_relations.basis: The existential certificate in the iff uses exactly CriticalDyadicBandIndex.
The global seam theorem applies the generic (d,E) collapse rowwise with E=seamUpperResetCharge.
The concrete charge bound discharges E≤2^(d+1) at every actual upper reset.
The endpoint transports the critical producer to the original all-band producer through the proved iff.
